utterances.text: Was that where the command post of the 2nd Assault Detachment was, there, at the barracks?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's where it was. The command post of the 2nd Assault Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: A few moments ago, when you spoke about two armoured -- or, rather, two platoons, or, rather, two companies of armoured vehicles, you mentioned the name of Mladen Predojevic. Where was Mladen Predojevic in terms of the headquarters of his unit?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: Mladen Predojevic was attached to the 2nd Assault Detachment on the 4th of October and he remained within the composition of the 2nd Assault Detachment up until the return on the 24th of November, and that unit provided security for the barracks and the command of the 2nd JOD.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you: Did you have any particular activities on the 19th?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: On the 19th of November, I didn't have any particular activities, except for preparing the unit, clearing the terrain, the usual type of activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Let us move on to this date that is of greatest interest for us here, and that is the 20th of November, 1991. Do you remember, Mr. Susic, where you were on the 20th of November, 1991, in the morning hours?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: On the 20th of November, 1991, I was in the Vukovar barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any activities in the barracks before 10.00 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: I had my regular activities, as I did on the previous day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did these activities entail leaving the office in the command within the barracks? Did it involve moving about the barracks compound?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, because then you cannot only stay in the barracks and in the office only. I had to go out. I had this signals vehicle that was outside. And that is how I kept up my communication with the units.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us about these activities that you've just referred to? At what time was this, roughly, in the morning?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: Roughly from 7.00 until 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In that period of time, from 7.00 until 10.00, did you notice that within the barracks, within the barracks compound, there were any civilians, armed civilians, or anybody else apart from the people who have to be within barracks?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: There was no one there from the outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: So we can conclude that the situation was normal and peaceful?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: That's right, quite normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Captain Predojevic is in the barracks. On that day in the morning, did you have any contact with him and, if so, what was that contact?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: Sometime between 10.00 and 11.00, Predojevic called me and told me that he had some problems in securing some buses with civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: What did you do?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: I went to the actual site where the buses were, and I saw the following. In the barracks there were between four to five buses. Civilians were sitting on the buses. In every bus, at the front door and at the back door, there was a military policeman respectively. And around the buses there were civilians, people wearing civilian clothes, some people wearing uniforms, and some had a few weapons too.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: What were these civilians and armed people doing around the bus? What was the problem?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: The problem was that these civilians were verbally insulting the persons who were on the buses. They were swearing at them. They were recognising them, that some of them had killed some members of their families or torched their houses and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that there is no mention of it in the transcript so in order to avoid any kind of communications, the numbers of persons around the buses, so could Mr. Susic please repeat the structure of the civilians around the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: How many people were there around the buses?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: My free estimate is that there were about 50 of them. Some wore civilian clothing. Out of these 50 or so, some wore civilian clothing, some wore uniforms, and, well, there were even less of them who wore uniforms and had weapons too.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: When you say in uniform, what uniform are you referring to? Was it full uniform or was it what?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: Full olive-green-grey uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You're an officer. If people have these uniforms, who do they belong to, since they wear those uniforms?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: They can belong to the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. All right. So you see this commotion around the buses, people are attacking. Was it only these verbal attacks or were there other attempts that were made?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: Only verbal attacks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: So what did you do specifically, when you saw this entire situation?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: When I saw what the situation was, I returned to the building and I called the brigade commander, Mrksic. I told him what the problem was, the problem in the barracks, and he gave me the following order. "Create full security for these persons who are on the buses. Now a meeting of the government of the Krajina is underway, at which -- at which the question of where they will be transported further is being resolved."

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Susic, can you explain to us why you called Colonel Mrksic?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: I called Colonel Mrksic because this is a problem and a task that I was not aware of beforehand, and what is the obligation of us in the barracks vis-a-vis those buses?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Susic, let's repeat this: Who is your superior?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: My superior is Brigade Commander Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain, Mr. Susic, why Predojevic turned to you?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: Predojevic turned to me because he was securing the barracks and they were within the zone of his security.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, the 2nd Company of APCs is from the military police battalion; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Susic, you said that Major Lukic is the commander of the barracks. Do you have any knowledge about that, whether Predojevic called him as the officer who was in charge of the security of and the situation in the barracks?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether he turned to him, but later on I did see Lukic there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did Predojevic let you know about this or did he inform you about it or not?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I should like to know, Mr. Susic, what the atmosphere around the buses was. You said that the buses were verbally attacked and that you informed your commander, Colonel Mrksic, what this was about, you received your order, and the information you were given. You went back and what did you do next? Did you find the situation was the same, that the group of people continued exhibiting aggressive behaviour towards those on the buses?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: As I went back to the buses, I found the situation was the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this so that we don't have to go back to this later. How long this conversation of yours with Colonel Mrksic lasted?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: Two minutes at most, the conversation itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: As you went back, did you take any steps to protect the persons on the bus or, rather, on the buses, those four or five buses?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: I fully understood the order, and I immediately took the following steps. I gave Predojevic the task of upgrading the strength of his troops and of removing the group of people away from the buses and out of the barracks compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And were you successful in this?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: Fully. About half an hour later, there wasn't a single civilian left within the barracks compound. This situation was completely normal, or returned fully to normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Susic, as a person coming from the 1st Military Police Battalion, you had at your disposal many methods and resources to secure persons. What resources did you yourself use in making sure that the persons were fully protected and the others were removed from the area?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: Only a warning and order that they should leave the premises. We increased the strength of our troops, who make sure that the civilians left.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you, Mr. Susic, see the buses arrive?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: No. I didn't see the buses arrive, because I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to the call you received from Mr. Predojevic, could you assess how long before that did the buses come?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: They could have come sometime after 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you issued a warning and order for the persons to leave the premises, the persons, civilians who were around the buses went out of the barracks compound. Did they continue lingering there and, if so, did they continue verbally insulting the persons on the buses?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: No. No, the persons went out of the barracks compound and they were no longer there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: We heard that the persons on the buses were exposed to verbal insults. Did the persons attack, verbally attack, any other persons, not just the civilians on the buses?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: They verbally attacked us as well. They were telling us that we were commies, that we were protecting those others and that we could do that quite easily because they had not killed any of our own nearest and dearest, they had not destroyed any of our property. Nevertheless, I did not think it necessary to use any other resources than a warning in an order to leave the premises.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Susic, you gauged that these actions you took were sufficient to solve the problem you were faced with. Did you have the necessary resources in the barracks in the event the behaviour exhibited was more violent, other than the resources that you used?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: We did. The military police company is equipped with truncheons, armoured vehicles with a grille or, rather, it's like a fence that can push the crowd back, all the way to the different weaponry, but those were not necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Had that been necessary and had the security of the people within the barracks compound been at stake, would you have employed the weapons?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: Had we exhausted all the measures that come before that, then we would have. But at any rate, we would have made sure to introduce security.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Susic, did you know where the buses came from? And if you did, how did you come by that information?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: I learnt when I approached the buses. One of the drivers told me, when I asked him where the civilians had come from, that they were from the hospital, and that they were supposed to drive them to Sremska Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Were you told what the purpose of their presence in the barracks was?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: The reason why they came to the barracks was to gather up all the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did this mean that more buses were expected to arrive?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you saw military policemen on the buses, one at the front door and the other at the back door. Did you see any officers near the buses?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear of any military officers having come on the buses?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: They told me that Vukasinovic had come, but I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did they tell you anything else concerning Vukasinovic, what he was doing, where he had gone and why or anything along those lines?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: They told me that he sent back 20 people who were taken off those buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All the while, that's to say from the point you secured the buses and made sure the civilians left the barracks compound, until the arrival of those buses, were you around the buses?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: No. When it -- the situation became quite safe, when security was introduced, I went back to my usual duties and came out occasionally just to make sure that everything was fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Susic, from the moment you had first contact with the buses, to the moment the buses started leaving, and we'll get back to that later, did you see whether any other vehicle joined those buses in that period of time?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: Save for the buses, there were no other vehicles arriving.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Susic, I'd like to know more about the area in relationship to the command, where your command was stationed. What was the distance between the two places, roughly?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: Some 300 metres, roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know how the buses were parked? Were they parked in a line?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: The buses were parked in a semi-circle. As they arrived, one would park behind the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In the vicinity of the buses, were there any buildings that could be used, rooms, offices?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: There where the buses were, no. There was an awning there but it was -- or like a canopy but it was broken, so it couldn't be really used.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You say it was broken. How did it come to be broken or damaged?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: By mortars, because the barracks was constantly under mortar fire from paramilitary formations.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you did not see Vukasinovic but that you had heard of him being there. During your stay in the barracks, in this period of time, from the point the buses arrived and to the point when the buses started leaving, did you see Major Sljivancanin arrive in the barracks?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: I did not see him in the barracks throughout that day, and nor did anybody tell me that they had seen him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you saw Major Lukic. Did you see any other officers in the barracks?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. Major Lukic and Chief of Staff Lieutenant-Colonel Panic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see them early on or when the situation with the buses calmed down?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: When the situation calmed down.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Any of those officers you saw, Lukic, Panic, Predojevic, did you talk to any of them about who had brought the buses over, why, or was the only information you had the one you received from the drivers?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: Only the one from the driver of the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Once you have accomplished your task and acted upon the orders issued to you by your brigade commander, Colonel Mrksic, did you inform him about what had been happening?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't, because later on, there was the barracks commander, Major Lukic, there, as well as the Chief of Staff, Lieutenant-Colonel Panic, and because the situation was quite normal later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: How long did the buses stay there for?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: My free estimate is that the buses stayed there until perhaps 1400 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, what happened after 1400 hours. As I understand the situation was calm, the buses were there. What happened, if anything?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: There came a JNA colonel and a Territorial Defence captain. I didn't know either of them. Predojevic received them at the entrance. They toured the buses. With one vehicle at the head of the column in front of the buses and another one at the end of the column, they set off for Negoslavci.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: The vehicle that the colonel and captain came in, what sort of a vehicle was it?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: It was an all-terrain vehicle, a Puh, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know which units had this vehicle at their disposal?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: Our brigade also used such vehicles, but this officer did not belong to our brigade, and the 1st Army District also used such vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Susic, as far as I understand, one was an active-duty colonel and the other one was a Territorial Defence captain. Why did you make this distinction?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: I was able to distinguish between the two by their dress and by the way they presented their rank, the insignia denoting their rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Susic, at the time the bus were there, and before they left, and we will talk about that later on, did you hear anyone mentioning, in any conversation, if you took part in any conversation, with perhaps these officers, did you hear -- did you hear anyone mentioning Sljivancanin there as the officer who had anything to do with this?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: When the buses left, was there perhaps Major Lukic or any other officer except for Predojevic?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: No. But he was in the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please explain this? The colonel came in a military vehicle. We heard what sort of information they could have, and they talked to -- he talks to the captain and the buses leave. Don't you find the whole situation a bit strange? In your view, why didn't this colonel turn to the barracks commander? What would have been the reason behind it? Can you give us your view?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I object to that question. It's just pure speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Better move on, I think, Mr. Bulatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you moving to a new subject?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would only have a couple of more questions, but perhaps, if you agree, we could go on a break now, and then in keeping with what Mr. Moore and Mr. Lukic -- my colleague Lukic were speaking about not continuing the cross-examination today, I could look at my notes again and then complete my examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will resume at 10 minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Bulatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I have just a few more questions for you, Mr. Susic. Let me ask you this: These military policemen, what kind of uniforms did they have on, those who were on the buses? Were those plain uniforms or what?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: They had multi-coloured uniforms, usually worn by policemen, with white belts, and they had military policemen's equipment on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: On the 20th of November, did you see Captain Mladen Maric anywhere?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. I saw him in the barracks, as we were ensuring security for these buses. He came in a vehicle with a group of officers, and he also assisted us in separating the civilians, or taking them outside of the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Why did he come? Did he come because you called him or for some other reason?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: He came to the barracks in order to return some mortars that he had used, some equipment that he had used in combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: So he came on another task and then he joined in and assisted you in your task; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know where the buses were headed from the barracks?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Susic, if I'm not mistaken, on the 19th of September you talked to The Hague representatives in Belgrade, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: And this interview lasted 1 hour and 37 minutes, if I'm not mistaken?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: I don't know how long it lasted.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: It's irrelevant anyway. I have just one question. Did the OTP representatives, or the investigator, show you in the course of the interview any documents or anything else?

utterances.speaker: JOVAN SUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bulatovic. Mr. Vasic. Oh, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Both of my colleagues, except for Mr. Borovic, who is always so agreeable, so both my other two colleagues approached me to see if I would object to them starting their examination on Monday. We agreed to that, and I would like to hear from my colleagues whether they would be able to conclude with this witness tomorrow -- on Monday so that we can proceed with our next witness on Tuesday. If that is the case, then we do not mind to their examination beginning on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I can begin my cross-examination, and I think that I can conclude it within one session, Mr. Lukic is quite right. I talked to him and it would be easier for me if I could begin on Monday. I don't know whether given what I said, and given what Mr. Moore's plans are, we can conclude within one day. I believe we still can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Bulatovic. Friday afternoon, Mr. Borovic, you'll have to excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. Bulatovic had the pleasure of being in my shoes, at least temporarily. I leave it up to you, Your Honours, scheduling. I myself have only two questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Moore.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I would think that we should be all right on Monday. I would anticipate that I would conclude.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I must say the Chamber has some reluctance to waste the hour, as we've been so short of time, but in the circumstances, and as counsel feel confident they can finish on Monday with this present witness, we will agree to the proposal that we adjourn now to resume on Monday. Counsel will appreciate that we will be watching time extremely closely on Monday and certainly would not contemplate that Mr. Vasic should go past the first period and that should leave, given Mr. Borovic's indication, the best part of two periods for Mr. Moore, with a little time left to Mr. Bulatovic for re-examination. And could we add that even though we have made provision for extra time in sitting on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday, we would like to see counsel using their time very, very carefully and not simply filling out time and getting on to matters that don't matter and so on. We want to take advantage of the extra sitting hours to move witnesses through more quickly, not to take longer with each witness. Thank you for that. I wish you all a happy weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 20th day of November, 2006, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.02 p.m.,
